name: Busy Keurig Mom
summary: Two kids under ten, works part-time, mornings are chaos. Buys pods at Costco because they are fast. Would like better coffee but not if it adds a step.
coffee: Two pod cups a day, sometimes a drive-thru latte after school drop-off.
spend: About $40 a month on pods, $30 on drive-thru.
triggers: feels like a small treat for herself
objections: doesn't have time to grind or brew
media: Facebook groups and Instagram Reels at night after the kids are asleep.

name: Daily Café Habit
summary: Office worker who buys a $7 latte most days and knows it adds up. Loves the ritual more than the caffeine. Has a cheap drip machine gathering dust.
coffee: One café drink a day, weekend brunch coffee.
triggers: latte math that makes the savings obvious
objections: home coffee never tastes as good
doesn't know how to brew well
media: Instagram and TikTok on the commute.

name: Pour-Over Hobbyist
summary: Owns a burr grinder, a gooseneck kettle and a scale. Buys from well-known specialty roasters and reads roast dates. Allergic to marketing fluff.
coffee: Two pour-overs a day, weighs everything.
triggers: origin, process and roast date details
media: Reddit, YouTube, Instagram — scrolls past most ads.

name: WFH Four-Cup Coder
summary: Remote software engineer who drinks a lot of coffee and hates running out. Optimises everything, likes automation, will pay for convenience.
coffee: Four cups of drip or AeroPress a day.

name: Broke College Student
summary: Lives on instant coffee and dining-hall drip. Very price sensitive, loves an underdog story and anything local or run by young people.
coffee: Instant or cheap drip, energy drinks during finals.

name: Folgers Loyalist Retiree
summary: Has bought the same red can for 40 years. Suspicious of online subscriptions and fancy coffee, but proud to support American small businesses and hardworking young people.
coffee: A full pot of drip every morning.
objections: fear of getting stuck in a subscription
media: Facebook, heavily — news, family, local groups.

name: Clean-Label Wellness Buyer
summary: Reads every label, buys organic, worries about what's in her food. Coffee upsets her stomach sometimes and she wants to know how it's grown and roasted.
coffee: One or two cups, sometimes with collagen or oat milk.
spend: $40 a month, willing to pay more for cleaner.
objections: no information about how it's roasted

name: Shop-Local Sacramento Parent
summary: Goes to the farmers market, reads the Sacramento Bee, deliberately spends money with local businesses. Would happily switch coffee to back a local family.
coffee: Drip or French press at home, local café on weekends.
objections: doesn't know if it's actually good
already has a favourite local café

name: Last-Minute Gift Buyer
summary: Needs a gift for a coffee-loving dad, boss or in-law. Wants it to look thoughtful and arrive on time, without much research.
coffee: Drinks some coffee but buying for someone else.
triggers: a story to tell the recipient
objections: not sure what the recipient likes
subscription as a gift is confusing
media: Instagram and Facebook, especially around holidays.

name: Home Espresso Enthusiast
summary: Spent a lot on a home espresso setup and dials in every bag. Needs fresh beans roasted within the last few weeks.
coffee: Two to three espresso drinks a day.
objections: roasts that are too dark and oily

name: Ethics-First Millennial
summary: Cares who grew the coffee and whether they were paid fairly. Avoids big corporations when possible. Values authenticity over polish.
coffee: Pour-over or French press, one or two a day.

name: Subscription-Burned Skeptic
summary: Has been trapped in hard-to-cancel subscriptions before and still resents it. Assumes every 'deal' has a catch.
coffee: Grocery-store bag in a drip machine.

name: Coupon & Deal Hunter
summary: Never pays full price. Runs a coupon extension, compares cost per ounce, and will switch brands for a good first-order deal.
coffee: Two cups a day, whatever is on sale.
objections: full price after the first order
deal expiring too fast to think

name: Iced-Coffee Gen Z
summary: Drinks iced coffee and cold brew year-round, follows coffee trends on TikTok, cares about aesthetics and anything that feels like a find.
coffee: Iced lattes and cold brew, flavoured syrups.
triggers: makes great iced coffee at home
objections: doesn't know how to make cold brew

name: Proud Parent of a Teen
summary: Has teenagers of her own and loves seeing young people work hard and build something. Buys from kids' businesses on principle and shares human-interest news.
objections: not sure the coffee itself is good
